cards.explanation: The answer is True. The text says Uzziah "…did what was right in the eyes of the LORD, just as his father Amaziah had done." (2 Chronicles 26:4) Amaziah was the king before him, so Uzziah had a pattern to follow. Sixteen years old and already walking straight, friends. I can't walk straight past a cooling rack.

The answer is success, friends. The text says, "…as long as he sought the LORD, God gave him success." (2 Chronicles 26:5) Notice the words "…as long as…" That little phrase is carrying the whole story on its back. Keep your eye on it.

The answer is that he builds cities, bakers. "Then he built cities near Ashdod and among the Philistines." (2 Chronicles 26:6) First the walls of Gath, Jabneh and Ashdod come down, then his own cities go up. Walls down, cities up, and I can't even finish a single tray of cookies without a snack break.

The answer is False. The text says, "God helped him against the Philistines, against the Arabs living in Gur-baal, and against the Meunites." (2 Chronicles 26:7) Uzziah had help, friends, and not the small kind. Remember who the helper was: God.

The answer is Egypt, friends. "…his fame spread as far as the border of Egypt, for he had become exceedingly powerful." (2 Chronicles 26:8) That's a long way for news to travel without a single group chat. Even the Ammonites were bringing him tribute. And the reason is right there in the verse: he had become exceedingly powerful.

The answer is stones, bakers. The devices were made "…to shoot arrows and catapult large stones from the towers and corners." (2 Chronicles 26:15) Arrows and big stones, all from up on the towers. I can barely get a cookie off the top shelf without a stool.

The answer is that he went in to burn incense on the altar himself, friends. The text says he "…entered the temple of the LORD to burn incense on the altar of incense." (2 Chronicles 26:16) He went in to do it himself. The next verses show why that was a big problem.

The answer is that he has no right to offer incense, bakers. They tell him, "Uzziah, you have no right to offer incense to the LORD." (2 Chronicles 26:18) Eighty priests plus Azariah is a whole lot of people to stand against a king. I think that took real courage.

The answer is False. The priests tell him, "…you have acted unfaithfully; you will not receive honor from the LORD God." (2 Chronicles 26:18) That's a hard thing to say to a king's face, friends. They said it anyway.

The answer is leprosy, friends. "…leprosy broke out on his forehead." (2 Chronicles 26:19) It happened while he was raging, right there before the altar of incense. This is a heavy part of the story. I think this one hurts.

The answer is that he hurries, bakers. "Indeed, he himself hurried to get out, because the LORD had afflicted him." (2 Chronicles 26:20) The priests rushed him, and he was hurrying too. A king who was raging in that room is now heading for the door fast.

The answer is True, friends. The text says, "…King Uzziah was a leper until the day of his death." (2 Chronicles 26:21) It's a sober line. The text says he lived in isolation and was cut off from the house of the LORD. I think it's a hard line to read.

The answer is his son Jotham, bakers. The text says Uzziah's "…son Jotham had charge of the royal palace and governed the people of the land." (2 Chronicles 26:21) The kingdom still needed someone running it while Uzziah lived apart. Jotham stepped up.

The answer is in a burial field of the kings, friends. He was "…buried near them in a field of burial that belonged to the kings, for the people said, “He was a leper.”…" (2 Chronicles 26:23) So he was laid near the kings, but in a field. That's how his story closes.
